chapter_theme: A song at Thirunageswaram (திருநாகேச்சுரம்): a catalogue of the wicked, from parent-revilers and adulterers to drunkards and hoarders, who will wander in the lowest births; the praise names Vayalur, where the Thiruppugazh was given, and Siva of the shrine as the father who praised his son as guru.

873.reading: Without any plea of his own, the poet lists the wicked who will wander in the lowest births like dogs: those who have no conduct and argue perversely, revile mother and father, kill the cow for its flesh, enjoy other men's wives without a qualm, live by every trick, drink intoxicating liquor, snatch the goods of the helpless without shame, babble their desire for what belongs to others, swagger with club, sword and bow, do sinful austerities without serving a guru, and hoard and bury wealth without giving. The praise names the vel that felled the one mango in the roaring sea, Murugan of Vayalur who received the true Thiruppugazh, the famed true guru whose teaching cuts the delusion of maya for those suffering from past deeds, praised by his father named Nagesa.
873.nuance: The song is a list of துட்டர்கள் rather than a confession, close to a moral code: the faults named are those the Kural also names (other men's wives, liquor, theft from the helpless, hoarding), with refusal of guru-service (குருசேவை கூடாத) among them. கோமாள நாயிற் கடைப்பிறப்பு: the punishment is birth as the lowest of dogs. மெய்த் திருப்புகழ் பெறு வயலூரா recalls Vayalur as the place of the Thiruppugazh itself. நாகேச நாமத் தகப்பன் is Siva of this shrine. The lines on ப்ராரத்த துக்கம் and புவி ஆதாரமாய்கைக்கு are hard to divide.

links.note: The Kural counts the man who heaps up wealth and does not use it as already dead; 873 puts those who hoarded and buried without giving (ஈயாது தேடிப் புதைத்த) among the wicked bound for the lowest births. Both condemn wealth withheld, the Kural as a life wasted, 873 as a sin with a sequel.

873 ends its list of the wicked with those who hoard and bury wealth without giving (ஈயாது தேடிப் புதைத்த துட்டர்கள்) and says they will wander in the lowest births, like dogs (கடைப்பிறப்பினில் உழல்வாரே). Kural 1002 says the delusion of clinging without giving (ஈயாது இவறும் மருள்) brings an unworthy birth (மாணாப் பிறப்பு). Both name the same fault and the same punishment, a low next birth for the one who does not give.
